output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by operators or the firmware. From 4 Oct, PackBridge sent a shelf-life value of 36 months for Veltranol instead of 24. That value came from a CC-309 edit made on 3 Oct, which was meant to take effect only from 1 Mar 2027, yet the system used it immediately. Every affected job matched its payload with no operator overrides, and jobs before 4 Oct were correct, including after the firmware change. Two lots from permanent day-shift staff on Line 1 are also affected, so the agency-operator explanation does not hold. Confidence is moderate (about 75%). The vendor says this cannot happen, so the exact reason the future-dated value was read is still unconfirmed. Next: put a hold on every Veltranol lot packed since 3 Oct, including the two in the warehouse; reset the Veltranol shelf-life record so only the approved value is read; add a second-person check of expiry at each setup; and review the other products changed under CC-309, especially HX-15-30 and MR-05-14. Do not discipline the agency staff or switch off the camera check.
